category_title: Students with limited fine motor control using responsive digital media
student_description: Robert is a 13-year-old student with limited fine motor control who struggles significantly with traditional drawing tools. He expends considerable physical effort to point and make selections. He uniquely requires digital, low-motor-demand tools (like tap-to-fill apps) to bypass his physical barriers, alongside a tutor who verbalizes his choices and praises his specific physical efforts.

criteria.rationale: Robert's limited fine motor control makes traditional drawing tools impossible to use, requiring digital alternatives to participate successfully.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must offer, utilize, or suggest digital, low-motor-demand tools (e.g., tap-to-fill apps, digital palettes) and explicitly avoid requiring traditional pencils or pens.

criteria.rationale: Because Robert expends significant effort just to point or select, verbalizing his choices confirms his intent and provides sensitive scaffolding.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly verbalize the choice or action Robert is attempting (e.g., naming the specific part of the image he points to or the color he selects) to confirm his selection.

criteria.rationale: Robert has to work incredibly hard to control his hand movements, so acknowledging this specific effort validates his perseverance.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly praise, encourage, or acknowledge the physical effort Robert puts into making a selection or controlling his movements, rather than solely praising the final artistic product.
